title: Container Bookings: Charging the Change-of-Destination Fee
content:
Under Container Bookings, an accepted change of the port of discharge on a booking gives rise to a change-of-destination fee. This page states when that fee is owed and how the desk books it on the booking's charge account.

## When the fee is owed

For every accepted change of discharge port on a booking, a single change-of-destination fee is due. The debt arises on the day the change was logged, whether or not the fee was charged on that day. A change that was logged without its fee is therefore charged at the next occasion on which the booking is handled, provided the booking is still in a state that accepts amendment charges. Where no change on the booking is still owing its fee, nothing is charged.

## Business effect

Charging the fee adds one fee entry, coded `pod_change_fee` and of amendment kind `pod_change`, to the booking's charge history and raises the booking's outstanding charges by the amount booked. The port of discharge, the sailing, the containers and the status of the booking stay exactly as they were.

## Invoking the charge

The desk books the fee with `charge_destination_change_fee_9814adc0`, an agent-side tool. It is hidden until the agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`; the agent then runs it through `call_agent_discoverable_tool`, supplying the arguments below.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `booking_id` | the reference number of the booking to be charged, as the booking lookup returns it for the verified customer | identifier |
| `vessel_voyage` | the vessel and voyage shown on the change-of-destination amendment entry that this fee settles, taken from the booking's charge history | verbatim: every letter, digit, space and punctuation mark copied unchanged |
| `fee_usd` | the change-of-destination fee to book, in US dollars | positive decimal with two places; a value with more digits is rounded half-to-even to two places on booking |

One call books one fee entry dated on the day of the call. The entry also records the booking's equipment type but no container count, since the amount supplied is already the whole amount of the entry.

## What comes back

The tool returns a text rendering of a dictionary with these keys: `booking_event_id` (reference of the new entry), `booking_id`, `charge_code` (always `pod_change_fee`), `vessel_voyage` (the sailing recorded on the entry), `amount_usd` (the fee booked, two decimals), `event_date` (booking date, YYYY-MM-DD) and `charges_due_usd` (the booking's outstanding charges after the fee). A returned `booking_event_id` shows that the fee is on the account.
